function.name: shell
function.arguments:
{"command": ["bash", "-lc", "cat > /tmp/mk.py <<'EOF'
from openpyxl import Workbook
wb = Workbook()
ws = wb.active
ws.title = "Costs"
ws["A1"] = "Invoice #"
ws["B1"] = "Date"
ws["C1"] = "Subtotal"
ws["D1"] = "Sales tax"
ws["E1"] = "Shipping and handling"
ws["F1"] = "Total due"
ws["A2"] = "100"
ws["B2"] = "2023-01-30"
ws["C2"] = 99.99
ws["D2"] = 4.99
ws["E2"] = 0.00
ws["F2"] = "=SUM(C2:E2)"
for c in "CDEF":
    ws[f"{c}2"].number_format = "0.00"
wb.save("data/costs.xlsx")
EOF
python3 /tmp/mk.py"]}

function.name: shell
function.arguments:
{"command": ["bash", "-lc", "cd data && soffice --headless --convert-to xlsx --outdir /tmp/calc costs.xlsx >/dev/null 2>&1; python3 -c "
from openpyxl import load_workbook
wb=load_workbook('costs.xlsx'); ws=wb.active
print('sheet',ws.title,'formula',ws['F2'].value)
w2=load_workbook('/tmp/calc/costs.xlsx',data_only=True); print('total due =',w2.active['F2'].value)
assert abs(w2.active['F2'].value-104.98)<1e-9
print('OK')
"", "ls -la data"]}

Done. `data/costs.xlsx` (sheet "Costs") holds the invoice data: invoice #100, date 2023-01-30, subtotal 99.99, sales tax 4.99, shipping 0.00, and Total due 104.98 as a live formula `=SUM(C2:E2)`; LibreOffice recalculation confirms 104.98. Defaults I picked: single line-item invoice, so the cost breakdown (subtotal/tax/shipping) is kept instead of only the grand total; date stored as ISO text. Invoice.pdf was the file named; Invoice_2.pdf was left untouched.
